gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 17?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current National Weather Service observations and forecast model consensus indicate New York City will reach a daily high of 80–81°F on August 16, driving the market’s 100% implied probability for that bin. To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble forecasts position Tokyo’s August 18 maximum near 30–32°C under mostly cloudy skies with isolated showers, supporting the market’s tight clustering around 31°C (41.5%) and 30°C (36.5%). Persistent Pacific high pressure maintains seasonal warmth across the Kanto plain, yet increased cloudiness limits surface heating while a moderate sea breeze from Tokyo Bay adds localized cooling. Urban heat-island effects and typical mid-August humidity amplify peaks, though short-range model runs show limited day-to-day variability. Updated JMA guidance and afternoon observations represent the next key data points that could shift positioning within these narrow temperature bands.

These conditions are expected to limit peak solar radiation and cap the maximum temperature near 25–27 °C, driving the closely matched market-implied odds for those outcomes. Subtle differences in convective timing, cloud cover thickness, and boundary-layer moisture could shift the daily high by 1–2 °C, while historical August averages near 22–23 °C provide climatological context for the uncertainty range reflected in trader consensus. Updated model runs and official observations from the Deutscher Wetterdienst will refine these projections ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency place Tokyo’s daily maximum near 32°C on August 17, yet persistent cloud cover, light showers, and elevated humidity are limiting solar heating and convective mixing, keeping observed readings closer to 29–30°C. Urban heat-island effects and the urban canopy normally amplify peaks in late summer, but today’s stable marine layer and reduced insolation introduce measurable downward pressure. Market-implied odds cluster tightly around 29–30°C because traders weigh the latest model consensus against real-time station data, recognizing that even modest increases in cloud thickness or earlier precipitation could cap the high below 31°C while clearer breaks could push it to 32°C. Resolution hinges on the official JMA observation at the primary Tokyo site.

Updated model runs and official NWS briefings tomorrow morning represent the primary near-term catalysts.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated model consensus and timing of any showers before peak heating hours remain key variables that could shift the final observed high.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecast models from European meteorological agencies point to a peak temperature in Munich shaped by an incoming Atlantic weather system delivering extensive cloud cover, thundery showers, and westerly winds that limit daytime insolation and advect cooler maritime air. These conditions suppress the urban heat island effect and reduce maximum readings relative to clear-sky climatology for mid-August, when highs typically reach 22–25°C. Model consensus shows modest spread around the 23–26°C range depending on exact shower timing and boundary-layer moisture, creating the tight market distribution across those bins as traders weigh the latest ECMWF and DWD runs against observational trends. Resolution hinges on the official highest instantaneous reading recorded by the Munich station network.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official guidance from the Met Office centers on a 24°C maximum for London on August 19, 2026, under partly cloudy skies with a chance of light showers or drizzle, following the recent heatwave that produced peaks above 34°C earlier in the month.** 

Post-heat spike conditions are turning more changeable, with models showing modest cooling and increased humidity that can limit afternoon heating through cloud cover or convective activity. This creates a plausible range of outcomes around the central forecast—sunny breaks could push readings into the mid-to-upper 20s, while thicker cloud or earlier rain would cap them near or below 23°C. 

The evenly distributed market-implied odds across 20–30°C bins reflect trader recognition of this short-range uncertainty, where small shifts in timing, wind patterns, or insolation can alter the daily high by several degrees before resolution. Historical August baselines near 21–22°C provide context, but current synoptic setup favors slightly above-average values with limited upside beyond the low-to-mid 20s.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models indicate mostly cloudy conditions over Tokyo on August 19, limiting daytime radiative heating and supporting maximum temperatures near the 30–32 °C range, consistent with the market’s clustered 19 % probabilities on those outcomes. Variable low-level moisture, possible scattered showers, and the urban heat-island effect introduce day-to-day spread of a few degrees, while the prevailing Pacific high maintains warm advection without extreme amplification. Historical mid-August variability around the 31 °C climatological normal further explains the flat distribution across 28–32 °C and the low odds assigned to outliers. Updated model runs and the next JMA three-hourly forecast will provide the clearest near-term signal for traders.

Historical August baselines near 21–22°C provide context, but current synoptic setup favors slightly above-average values with limited upside beyond the low-to-mid 20s.

Variable low-level moisture, possible scattered showers, and the urban heat-island effect introduce day-to-day spread of a few degrees, while the prevailing Pacific high maintains warm advection without extreme amplification. Historical mid-August variability around the 31 °C climatological normal further explains the flat distribution across 28–32 °C and the low odds assigned to outliers. Updated model runs and the next JMA three-hourly forecast will provide the clearest near-term signal for traders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to a daily maximum of 25–27 °C in Munich on August 17, 2026, because short-range numerical weather prediction models, including consensus runs from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and Global Forecast System, indicate modest surface heating under a mix of broken cloud and scattered thundery showers. These conditions limit insolation and evaporative cooling while steering a cooler maritime air mass across southern Germany, keeping afternoon temperatures well below the late-summer climatological mean of roughly 23–25 °C. Morning observations already near 21 °C, combined with westerly flow and 60–80 % relative humidity, further constrain the potential for rapid warming. Market pricing reflects genuine forecast uncertainty around the precise timing and coverage of convective activity rather than any strong signal for either a cooler or hotter outlier day. Updated model guidance and observational data from the Deutscher Wetterdienst are expected to refine these probabilities through the afternoon.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to a daily maximum of 25–27 °C in Munich on August 17, 2026, because short-range numerical weather prediction models, including consensus runs from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and Global Forecast System, indicate modest surface heating under a mix of broken cloud and scattered thundery showers. These conditions limit insolation and evaporative cooling while steering a cooler maritime air mass across southern Germany, keeping afternoon temperatures well below the late-summer climatological mean of roughly 23–25 °C. Morning observations already near 21 °C, combined with westerly flow and 60–80 % relative humidity, further constrain the potential for rapid warming. Market pricing reflects genuine forecast uncertainty around the precise timing and coverage of convective activity rather than any strong signal for either a cooler or hotter outlier day. Updated model guidance and observational data from the Deutscher Wetterdienst are expected to refine these probabilities through the afternoon.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the LaGuardia Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/ny/new-york-city/KLGA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service model consensus and early surface observations for August 17, 2026, position 82–85°F as the dominant range by showing neutral-to-slightly-below-average conditions relative to the 1991–2020 Central Park baseline of 83°F. Stable high pressure, light winds, and limited moisture advection have suppressed stronger daytime heating, while modest cloud cover has capped peak solar insolation. Updated short-range guidance from the National Weather Service and ensemble means indicate little potential for rapid afternoon warming or convective cooling that would shift outcomes outside the 80–87°F window. With the observation window closing soon, trader-implied probabilities reflect high confidence in these moderate readings over rarer extremes.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from the UK Met Office and ensemble guidance shows a transition from the mid-August heatwave (peaking near 38 °C on 13 August) to more typical changeable Atlantic flow, with a trough and associated showers expected to limit daytime warming on 19 August. Official guidance currently projects a maximum of 24 °C under partly cloudy skies with scattered showers possible, keeping the daily high in the 23–25 °C range; slight variations in timing or coverage of cloud and rain explain the tight clustering of market-implied odds around these three outcomes. Longer-range runs indicate modest uncertainty in exact steering and moisture transport, but no strong signal supports either a return to hotter anticyclonic conditions or significantly cooler northerly flow by mid-week. Traders are therefore weighting the most probable Met Office forecast values while discounting tail risks below 22 °C or above 26 °C.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Short-range forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency indicate mostly cloudy skies over Tokyo on August 19, 2026, with daytime highs expected near 31–33°C amid persistent Pacific High influence and typical summer humidity levels exceeding 70%. This aligns with the broader seasonal outlook for above-normal temperatures across eastern Japan, following multiple extremely hot days earlier in the summer. Model consensus emphasizes limited cooling from cloud cover or sea breezes, while the urban heat island effect supports readings in the low 30s. Trader sentiment, reflected in 31°C leading at 41.5% implied probability, centers on these JMA guidance and ensemble runs, with updates from daily briefings and global models likely to refine the exact maximum before resolution.
